\textbf{(a)} Let $u=\sec\frac x3$, $du=\frac13\sec\frac x3\tan\frac x3\,dx$, $\tan^2=u^2-1$; $u$ runs from $1$ to $\sec\frac\pi3=2$:
\[3\int_1^2(u^2-1)\,du=3\Big[\frac{u^3}3-u\Big]_1^2=3\Big(\frac23+\frac23\Big)=\boxed{4}.\]
\textbf{(b)} $x^2+2x+10=(x+1)^2+9$ and $x=(x+1)-1$:
\[\int_{-1}^2\frac{x+1}{(x+1)^2+9}dx-\int_{-1}^2\frac{dx}{(x+1)^2+9}=\Big[\tfrac12\ln((x+1)^2+9)-\tfrac13\tan^{-1}\tfrac{x+1}{3}\Big]_{-1}^2\]
\[=\tfrac12\ln18-\tfrac13\cdot\tfrac\pi4-\tfrac12\ln9=\boxed{\tfrac12\ln2-\tfrac{\pi}{12}}\approx0.0848.\]
3:
Split into the rectangle $0\le x\le3$, $-2\le y\le2$ (area 12, centroid $x=1.5$) and the half-disk of radius 2 to the right of $x=3$ (area $2\pi$, centroid $x=3+\frac{4\cdot2}{3\pi}=3+\frac{8}{3\pi}$):
\[\bar x=\frac{12(1.5)+2\pi\big(3+\frac{8}{3\pi}\big)}{12+2\pi}=\boxed{\frac{18+6\pi+\frac{16}{3}}{12+2\pi}}\approx2.307.\]
5:
Measure height $y$ from the ground; the sphere's center is at $y=R$. A slice at height $y$ ($0\le y\le R$) is a disk of radius$^2$ $R^2-(y-R)^2=2Ry-y^2$. Its mass is $1000\pi(2Ry-y^2)\,dy$ kg and it is lifted from the ground to height $y$:
\[W=\int_0^R9.8\cdot1000\pi(2Ry-y^2)\,y\,dy=9800\pi\Big[\frac{2Ry^3}{3}-\frac{y^4}{4}\Big]_0^R=9800\pi\cdot\frac{5R^4}{12}=\boxed{\frac{12250\pi}{3}R^4\ \text{J}}.\]
8:
Reading the graph: on $[4,6]$ $f$ is the line from $(3,2.5)$ to $(6,1)$, so $f(4)=2$ and the slope is $-\frac12$; on $[6,10]$ it is the upper half of the circle of radius 2 centered at $(8,1)$.

\textbf{(a)} $\int_4^6f=\frac{2+1}{2}\cdot2=3$; $\int_6^{10}f=\underbrace{4\cdot1}_{\text{rectangle}}+\underbrace{\tfrac12\pi(2)^2}_{\text{half disk}}=4+2\pi$. Average:
\[\frac{1}{6}(7+2\pi)\approx\boxed{2.214}.\]
\textbf{(b)} $g(x)=\int_{x^2}^7f(t)\,dt$, so $g'(x)=-f(x^2)\cdot2x$ and
\[g''(x)=-2f(x^2)-4x^2f'(x^2).\]
At $x=2$: $g''(2)=-2f(4)-16f'(4)=-2(2)-16(-\tfrac12)=\boxed{4}$.
10:
Logistic equation with capacity 30: $P(t)=\dfrac{30}{1+Ae^{-30kt}}$. $P(0)=1\Rightarrow A=29$. $P(4)=5$: $1+29e^{-120k}=6\Rightarrow e^{-120k}=\frac5{29}\Rightarrow 30k=\frac{\ln(29/5)}{4}$.

Half the students: $P=15\Rightarrow 29e^{-30kt}=1\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{\ln29}{30k}=\dfrac{4\ln29}{\ln(29/5)}\approx\boxed{7.66\ \text{hours}}$.
